message: Running command: cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul && grep -rn "SMALL_XML" ext/ox/*.h ext/ox/*.c

message.content:
Now I understand! The XML string is copied into a **stack buffer** using `ALLOCA_N` when `len <= SMALL_XML`. This is the "Dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow" — the buffer is a dynamically-sized stack allocation (alloca).

So the buffer `xml` is on the stack (via alloca). `pi.str = xml`, `pi.end = xml + len - 1`, `pi.s = xml`.

Now, in `read_text`, when it hits `\0`, `pi->s` points one past the `\0`. The `\0` is at position `len-1` (the last byte of the copied buffer, since `memcpy(xml, x, len)` copies `len` bytes including the `\0`). So `pi->s` points to `xml + len`, which is **one past the end of the stack buffer**.

Then in `_ox_err_set_with_location`, `current = pi->s = xml + len`, and `xml < current` is true. The loop reads `*current` which is `xml[len]` — one byte past the end of the stack buffer → **Dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ 1**.

So the PoC needs to trigger `read_text` to hit a `\0` (end of string) and call `set_error`. Let me figure out the exact input.

Let me check `SMALL_XML` value.
